complexity_ledger.narrative: specs/results/scorecards/score-drives-validation/GOAL-scored-at-goal-time/SV-07/RESULT.md is the evidence ledger; `references/scoring_validation.md` (SV-02) is the design this ticket was sent to implement. WHAT THE TICKET WAS ASKED FOR. SV-02 found one property that separates well-validated from badly-validated code without grading which tools made the tests, priced three carriers for it against the real renderer, and defended the cheapest -- sharpening the recorded-note prompt that already elicits it, at minus fifteen bytes and no new rung. The work order said ship that, and bound it with three constraints: do not restore a retired dimension, do not add a rung, do not force a card bump. WHAT CAME BACK. The prompt is built and prices at exactly the figure SV-02 predicted, and it cannot go into the card at this ticket. A recorded note's prompt is inside BOTH of the card's seals -- the payload `load_rubric` digests, and the bytes `serve` emits, which the version history declares per version. Put the priced prompt in and change nothing else, and the card's own change rule refuses it: bump the card, or restore the text. The card's own version 5 row is the precedent, because it moved no anchor, moved only served bytes, and took a bump to do it. So BOTH carriers cost a version bump, which was the decisive argument SV-02 used against the rung. Filed as SV-07-DF-01 and not fixed, because the work order says a required bump is a finding and not a licence, and because the bump additionally owes the change rule's re-score of a prior example under both versions, which is a judging round and belongs to the evaluation ticket. WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD, at zero bytes on the served surface. `scripts/candidate_note_bar.py` derives the candidate bar from the card at run time, applies exactly one substitution, adds the version row the change rule requires, and prices the result with the real renderer: 6,281 to 6,266 bytes, 9 to 9 rungs, anchors digest byte-identical, exactly one served line moved. A generator and not a checked-in frozen copy, because the one-home test measured that three of four disagreeing copies of this card went uncaught by the whole suite, and there is nothing yet to compare a FUTURE candidate against. It makes SV-02's one missing experiment runnable in one command instead of by hand-freezing a file. THE DEMONSTRATED FAILING INPUT IS ON REAL SEALED CARDS AND NOT A FIXTURE. The two version-5 cards under close-the-loop-cl03-v5 agree with the shipped bar today and drift against the candidate on both seals -- served drift 46 to 48, rubric drift 66 to 68, the same two cards each time -- while the same cards checked against the shipped bar do not drift, so the drift is a fact about the candidate and not about the cards. WHAT WAS REJECTED. Restoring the retired dimension; adding any rung; bumping the card; a checked-in frozen candidate; a checker that a note carries a denominator, which SV-02 rejected under the no-new-gates rule; and productionising SV-02's `demonstration_grade`, which its own page says has never been validated against a human read. No skill was edited and `skill-manager sync` was never run.

ticket.objective: PLACEHOLDER. Scope is defined by SV-06 and SV-02 and this ticket is REWRITTEN FROM THEIR DESIGNS BEFORE DISPATCH. Implement the cross-skill changes so a project being onboarded scores as part of the GOAL PROCESS rather than as a separate evaluation act. Nothing is settled: SV-06 decides which of the four files change, where in the lifecycle the score belongs, what crosses a skill boundary, and how it behaves for a project that declines to score; SV-02 decides whether validation is scorable at all, AND IF ITS ANSWER IS NO THIS TICKET'S SCOPE SHRINKS TO ARCHITECTURE, WHICH IS A LEGITIMATE OUTCOME. What holds regardless: the card is NEVER MANDATORY and absence is designed for first; no new gates; a goal that cannot be scored is not a goal that fails; it must work for a project that is not this one, tested the way CL-04 tested the loop; the served surface must not grow; R1 on a real subject; and SKILLS ARE READ NOT EDITED -- anything that must change in SKILL_MANAGER_HOME is PROPOSED AS A DIFF AND ESCALATED, never applied, and skill-manager sync is never run.
